title: Generation, culture, and stimulation of small intestinal murine organoids in parasitology research
author: Campillo Poveda, Drurey, et al.
materials: Goat anti-rabbit IgG (H + L) secondary antibody, FITC
Ulex europaeus (gorse) agglutinin I (UEA I), fluorescein (FITC)

steps.title: Collect proximal small intestine tissue
steps.instruction: Dissect the most proximal 10 cm of the small intestine, flush with 5 mL ice‑cold PBS using a 5 mL syringe and a 200 µL tip, cut longitudinally, wash out remaining contents, gently scrape the upper mucosa with a coverslip, transfer tissue to a 50 mL Falcon tube containing 15 mL ice‑cold PBS and keep on ice during transport to the laboratory.

steps.title: Wash and mince intestinal tissue
steps.instruction: In a biosafety hood, transfer the tube contents to a Petri dish, cut the gut into 1–2 mm pieces with scissors, move pieces to a fresh 50 mL Falcon tube, add ice‑cold PBS to a final volume of 10 mL, pipette up/down gently ten times, allow fragments to settle, discard PBS, and repeat the wash two more times.

steps.title: EDTA incubation to release crypts
steps.instruction: Aspirate PBS, add 20 mL ice‑cold PBS containing 2 mM EDTA, and incubate on a roller for 30 min at 4 °C. After incubation, let tissue fragments settle, aspirate the PBS‑EDTA, add 10 mL ice‑cold PBS, mix gently ten times, and let fragments settle again.

steps.title: Collect and assess crypt fractions
steps.instruction: Collect the supernatant (Fraction 1) into a 15 mL tube, repeat the gentle pipetting and collection until six fractions are obtained, taking 20 µL from each fraction into a 96‑well plate to examine crypt concentration under a 4× objective; retain crypt‑enriched fractions (typically Fractions 2–6).

steps.title: Filter and centrifuge crypts
steps.instruction: Combine the selected fractions, pass them through a 70 µm cell strainer into a 50 mL Falcon tube, wash the strainer with 5 mL ice‑cold PBS, then centrifuge at 300 g for 3 min at 4 °C using a swing‑out rotor. If crypts do not pellet, add ~10 mL ice‑cold PBS and repeat at 400 g.

steps.title: Prepare Matrigel and resuspend crypts
steps.instruction: Thaw Matrigel (MG) on ice (or at 4 °C) to keep it liquid, remove the supernatant from the crypt pellet, add 10 mL ADF Base, transfer to a 15 mL Falcon tube, spin at 100 g for 3 min at 4 °C to remove single cells, discard supernatant, add another 10 mL ADF Base, take 20 µL to count crypts, then spin the remaining suspension at 300 g for 3 min at 4 °C and resuspend the pellet in MG (≈500 µL is sufficient for ~12 wells).

steps.title: Plate crypts in Matrigel domes
steps.instruction: Working quickly to prevent MG solidification, dispense 50 µL of the MG‑crypt suspension into each well of a pre‑warmed (37 °C) 24‑well plate (≈500 crypts per well), then incubate the plate for 10 min at 37 °C to allow the MG domes to solidify.

steps.title: Add organoid growth medium and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL per well of ADF Org medium supplemented with EGF, R‑spondin, Noggin and ChiR to the side of each well so the MG dome is not disturbed, and place the plate in a 37 °C incubator.

steps.title: Change medium on day two
steps.instruction: On day 2, gently remove the existing medium without disrupting the MG domes, then add 500 µL per well of fresh ADF Org medium containing EGF, R‑spondin and Noggin (ChiR omitted), and return the plate to 37 °C. Prior to all steps, briefly rinse Falcon tubes, tips and serological pipettes with ADF Base to prevent tissue adhesion.

steps.title: Capture organoid morphology images
steps.instruction: Acquire bright‑field images of organoids using an inverted microscope or EVOS system with 4×, 10×, and/or 20× objectives, then quantify morphological changes with ImageJ or similar software.

steps.title: Prepare organoid single‑cell suspension for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Harvest organoids, dissociate them to single cells, and count viable cells before staining.

substeps.instruction: Replace medium with 1 mL cold ADF Base and scrape with a 10 mL serological pipette to detach MG.
Transfer the MG‑containing suspension to a 15 mL Falcon tube, bring the volume to 10 mL with cold ADF Base, and centrifuge at 300 g for 4 min.
Aspirate supernatant and gently disrupt the pellet with a P200 pipette (≈10 gentle strokes).
Add 0.5–1 mL TrypLE Express plus DNase II (2000 U/mL); use 0.75 mL for three wells or 0.5 mL for two wells.
Incubate at 37 °C for 20–25 min on a shaker to dissociate organoids.
Inactivate TrypLE by adding 5 mL ADF Base containing 5 % FCS.
Pipette the suspension 5–10 times to obtain a cloudy single‑cell suspension.
Pass the suspension through a 40 µm cell strainer.
Count cells with trypan blue; aim for ~2 × 10⁴ cells per well for flow analysis.
Spin at 400 g for 5 min, resuspend in PBS, and plate 100 µL per well into a 96‑well round‑bottom plate.
Spin again at 400 g for 5 min at 4 °C and wash once with 100 µL PBS.

steps.title: Stain organoid cells for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Perform live/dead discrimination, blocking, surface and intracellular antibody staining, and fixation.

substeps.instruction: Incubate cells with BV506 live/dead dye (1:1000 dilution, 100 µL per well) for 30 min at 4 °C in the dark.
Spin 400 g for 5 min, discard supernatant, and wash with 200 µL PBS.
Block with rat IgG (1:50 dilution, 50 µL per well) for 20 min at 4 °C.
Add 150 µL FACS buffer, mix, spin 400 g for 5 min, and discard supernatant.
Stain extracellular antigens with 50 µL antibody mix (typically 1:200 dilution) for 35 min at 4 °C in the dark (use Brilliant Stain Buffer if required).
Wash with 150 µL PBS, spin 400 g for 5 min.
Fix cells by adding 100 µL 4 % PFA, incubate 15 min at room temperature.
Spin, wash once with 200 µL PBS.
Permeabilize with 150 µL PBS containing 1 % Triton X‑100 for 15 min at room temperature.
Stain intracellular antibodies in 50 µL PBS + 1 % BSA for 1 h at room temperature in the dark.
If secondary antibodies are needed, wash with 150 µL permeabilization buffer, then incubate with 50 µL secondary antibodies for 30 min at room temperature in the dark.
Wash twice with 200 µL FACS buffer and keep cells in FACS buffer until acquisition.
Acquire data on a flow cytometer (or sort desired populations).

steps.title: Indirect immunofluorescence staining of organoids
steps.instruction: Fix, permeabilize, and stain intact organoids on slides for microscopy.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate medium, wash wells twice with cold PBS, and fix with 4 % paraformaldehyde for 20 min at room temperature.
Rinse once with PBS, add 500 µL PBS per well, wrap with parafilm, and store at 4 °C (up to 2 weeks).
Permeabilize with PBS containing 0.5 % Triton X‑100 for 10 min at 4 °C.
Rinse three times with PBS + 100 mM glycine (10–15 min per wash) at room temperature.
Incubate with 200 µL per well of IF buffer for 45–60 min at room temperature.
Add primary antibody diluted in Antibody Dilution Buffer and incubate overnight (15–18 h) at room temperature.
Rinse three times with IF buffer (5–10 min each) at room temperature with gentle rocking.
Incubate with fluorescent secondary antibody in Antibody Dilution Buffer for 40–50 min at room temperature.
Rinse once with IF buffer (5 min) with gentle rocking.
Rinse 2–3 times with PBS (5 min each) at room temperature.
Remove chambers from slides.
Apply DAPI (1:10 000 in water) for 10 min at room temperature.
Rinse 2–3 times with PBS (5 min each) at room temperature.
Mount coverslips with VECTASHIELD mounting medium.

steps.title: Extract RNA from organoids
steps.instruction: Lyse organoids with Trizol and purify RNA using a column kit.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate medium from each well and wash with 400 µL ice‑cold PBS.
Add 400 µL Trizol to each well, incubate on ice for 10 min to dissolve Matrigel.
Pipette up/down to fully dissolve MG and transfer the lysate to an Eppendorf tube.
Vortex 10 s, then store at –80 °C until further processing.
Centrifuge at 12 000 g for 2 min at 4 °C and transfer the clear supernatant to a new tube.
Add 100 µL chloroform, mix well, and incubate at room temperature for 3 min.
Centrifuge at 12 000 g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Transfer the upper aqueous phase to a fresh tube, avoiding interphase material.
Add 1.5 volumes of 100 % ethanol, invert several times to mix.
Proceed with RNA purification using the RNeasy Mini Kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
